A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ERMoE and ERMoE-ba. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite layout changes and added supplementary sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, image-text retrieval, and ADNI brain-age experiments, together with routing analyses, calibration experiments, and parameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds component ablations, routing-cost measurements, expert-count scaling, an Expert-Choice comparison, and text-tower fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the expert factorization, cosine scoring, thresholded top-k routing, fallback, orthogonality objective, and MRI adaptation. The newly specified re-orthonormalization frequency documents an existing operation rather than establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover ImageNet, CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet, COCO, Flickr30K, and ADNI. The additions concern component controls, model configurations, and training settings; no new dataset, population, domain, or task is reported.

E2.justification: Appendix Section 13 adds an evaluated Expert-Choice baseline on ImageNet, reporting 78.95% top-1 versus ERMoE's 88.03%. Expert-Choice was cited but not evaluated in this comparison in v1. Existing benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New diagnostic protocols include component controls at fixed E, k, and T, load CV² and routing-only cost measurements, a one-layer, one-epoch memory test at E=8 and E=32, and fine-tuning Fix-CLIP's text tower. These extend the settings without revising the original benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained threshold, top-k, orthogonality-weight, calibration, and anatomical analyses, v2 directly ablates standard versus eigenparameterized experts, learned versus cosine routing, and removal of orthogonality. Routing-overhead, expert-count scaling, and text-tuning analyses also substantially extend the tests of mechanism and practicality.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new load CV² measures imbalance across experts, rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and S1–S2 retain their values, but substantial diagnostic results are added. Table S3 reports 94.12%, 91.07%, and 95.35% accuracy for standard weights, learned routing, and λ=0, versus 96.05% for ERMoE. Table S4 adds routing costs of 1.169 G FLOPs/0.05 ms versus V-MoE's 0.631 G/0.03 ms. Scaling, Expert-Choice, and fine-tuned Fix-CLIP results are also new; the latter uses a different training setting.

T1.justification: Appendix Section 11 adds asymptotic claims for routing computation, O(BEdr), routing-state memory, O(Edr²), and re-orthonormalization cost, O(Edr²) per epoch. Existing mathematical definitions and equations remain unchanged; no proof is added.

C1.justification: The shortened abstract preserves the claims of eigenbasis-aligned routing, stable utilization without balancing losses, strong classification/retrieval performance, and anatomically interpretable brain-age prediction. The introduction's contributions and conclusion retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: The new appendix attributes most gains to cosine alignment, additional gains to eigenparameterization, and mainly stability benefits to orthogonality. It acknowledges extra routing arithmetic, identifies dispatch and expert computation as scaling bottlenecks, and interprets text-tower tuning as beneficial for retrieval.

D1.justification: v1 describes occasional re-orthogonalization; v2 specifies once-per-epoch re-orthonormalization and explicitly states that no online d×d eigendecomposition is performed. These are added implementation disclosures. The code URL and ADNI access information are substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and the same 53 referenced works are retained. Newly evaluating the already cited Expert-Choice method does not otherwise revise the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the abstract, revises the author and equal-contribution block, adds email addresses and acknowledgments, and appends Sections 10–14. Most existing scientific prose and the narrative order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds component-ablation Table S3 and routing-cost Table S4, relocates existing displays such as Figure 1, and adjusts algorithm placement and pagination. Existing figures, captions, and benchmark table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Table S3 provides direct evidence about the central components, while Table S4 isolates routing overhead previously obscured by aggregate efficiency reporting. These improve mechanism attribution and cost transparency. The gains remain limited by terse experimental details, absent uncertainty estimates, and ambiguous scaling language: Section 12's 2.2 GB is the increase in the method–baseline memory gap, from 2.5 to 4.7 GB, rather than either absolute overhead.
